title: Cornet versus trumpet tone today
summary: The cornet has a rounder, mellower tone; he disliked the trumpet's feel.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Is the cornet being used very much this day, today, outside of Dixieland jazz?

XXXXXXXNXTONYX Yes, a lot of bandsman used them in the highschool and college bands, but no so much as trumpet. Trumpet is more or less, it's more piercing, has a more piercing tone where the cornet has a more round and mellow tone.
That's correct. Other than that they blow.....
Does that have to do with the longer length of the trumpet? That gives it that shriller tone?

Yes. Yes. And the cornet is shorter and it also has to do with the bore of the horn. They have a small, medium and a large bore horns and trumpets and cornets. But a cornet, well it's the only thing I've ever played. I tried a trumpet once but I didn't like it. It didn't.... ...

No, I didn't like the sound. I didn't like the feel of the way it sits out, too far out. Whereas my elbows are close to my body this way and I feel more comfortable. You know, that's the way it is with horns. Some guys get used to the trumpet.
Yes because some of them make almost a fettish of stretching it way out here somewhere. (LAUGHTER).
I like it close and comfortable.
